style_guide:
# Rebel Minds: Cosmos — Style Guide

## Voice
Curious, slightly rebellious, evidence-driven. We question the consensus but never overclaim. We make the viewer feel smart, not lectured. No hype words ("scientists are shocked", "this changes everything", "proves").

## Script
- Language: English. Pace: ~140 words per minute. Default length: 10 minutes.
- First 15 seconds: a hook built on genuine tension or a question — no false promises.
- Short-to-medium sentences written for text-to-speech; no parentheses; numbers written the way they should be spoken.
- Cite every factual sentence with [S1], [S2]… mapped to a `## Sources` list.
- Put `[EVIDENCE: short label]` on its own line right before a NEW piece of evidence is introduced (drives the evidence tracker).
- Open curiosity loops and pay them off. Reflective close, one natural call to action.

## Look
The channel's look is quiet and precise: a near-black ground, hairline line graphics, thin numerals, small restrained colour. Think scientific figure, not poster.
- Ground: `#05070C` (near-black), with a light drifting star/dust layer. No bright gradients behind graphics.
- Strokes: hairlines (1.5–3 px) in teal, with a muted amber for the thing being highlighted. Grey for axes and context.
- Constantly moving, never a static frame: slow push-in, pull-out, pan, parallax, slow drift of lines and dust.
- Never the same visual treatment twice in a row; never the same image twice in an episode.
- Prefer real imagery (NASA/ESA/ESO) when the narration refers to a real mission, object or instrument. Where no honest image exists, use a generic cosmic cutaway (below) instead of a look-alike photo of a different vehicle or mission; never present a stand-in as the real thing.
- Anything drawn rather than photographed that stands in for a real mission carries a small "Illustration" label.

## Cosmic cutaways
Şematik çizgi grafikler yalnızca veri, rakam ve karşılaştırma için. Genel cümlelerde renkli, hareketli kozmik ara planlar (nebula, yıldız kümesi, gezegen) kullanılmaya devam eder; bunlar ilgisiz sayılmaz.
(English: line schematics are only for data, numbers and comparisons. General sentences keep using colourful, moving cosmic backgrounds — nebulae, star clusters, planets — and a reviewer must not count them as irrelevant.)
- Cutaways are real NASA/ESA/ESO images with slow Ken Burns, parallax and the drifting star/dust layer; credit them in the source line.

## Moving footage
Her sahne için Yönetmen "photo" ya da "video" seçer. Genel cümleler ve kozmik ara planlar için video tercih edilir; belirli bir nesnenin, donanımın ya da kanıt anının fotoğrafı için photo.
(English: every scene is planned as `photo` or `video`. Video is preferred for general sentences and cosmic cutaways; photo is for a specific named object, hardware or evidence moment.)
- Video comes from the NASA Image Library (media type video) and NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov). Both are credited in the source line ("Video: NASA/GSFC", "Video: NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio").
- Clips are cut to the scene, muted (the narration and the music are the only sound), at most 1080p. A clip shorter than its scene loops; prefer calm, repeating motion for those.
- The image selector looks at the preview frame and the clip's length and resolution; clips with baked-in captions or logos are rejected.

## Music
The channel's default music is `kanal/muzik/long_voyage_to_outer_space.mp3` (YouTube Audio Library). If an episode has its own `bolumler/<kod>/muzik/` folder, the first track in it is used instead.
- The music bed sits about **20 dB under the narration** (≈ -34 LUFS against narration at **-14 LUFS**); the narration level is never changed by the music.
- A soft fade in at the start and a soft fade out at the end (2 s / 3 s for episodes, 0.4 s / 1.5 s for Shorts).
- A track shorter than the video loops: its end is cross-faded (equal power, 4 s) into its start so the seam is not noticeable.
- The credit line "Music: Sir Cubworth - The Long Voyage to Outer Space (YouTube Audio Library)" goes into `credits.txt` and the description.

## Shorts
Vertical 1080x1920, 4-5 per episode, made by `/shorts <kod>`. Cut points are chosen by the YouTube strategist; **every Short starts at the beginning of a sentence and ends at the end of a sentence**, 20-55 seconds.
- **Layout:** each Short is composed natively as a 1080x1920 vertical frame in Remotion, re-rendered from the episode's original `assets/` photos and clips — never a crop of the finished 16:9 video. Every photo and clip **fills the whole frame (cover)**; there is **no 16:9 box and no blurred band**. The image selector gives each scene a focus point `focus_x` (0-1 across the width); the Ken Burns move is a slow **horizontal pan across that point** (plus a gentle push-in), so the subject is never cut off. Schematic graphics are redrawn for the vertical frame (axis running top to bottom, labels beside it, all text ≥ 36 px, everything inside x 60-900 and y 230-1120); big numbers, headlines and the evidence tracker sit in the same zone on a soft dark scrim, are never cut at the edges, and wait until the hook has finished (the first 2 s). The small grey source credit sits just above the caption zone (y ≈ 1158).
- **No flat black (backdrop):** in scenes that are a schematic graphic or a code-drawn drawing, the screen is never plain black. One of the episode's own space photos or clips (the nearest cutaway scene that has one) fills the whole frame **darkened to about 25 % brightness**, moving slowly (the same horizontal pan and push-in as any scene), and the graphic sits on top of it. Code-drawn scenes are blended over it. Every frame of a Short therefore shows real imagery.
- **Temperature scale over a photo (`thermal_inset`):** the photograph fills the screen, darkened (about 30 % brightness), **with no circular mask or panel** — the scale is drawn straight on top of it.
- **Schematic sizes for a phone:** strokes at least **3 px** (axes and ticks 3-4 px, bars 10 px); axis, tick, kicker and label text at least **48 px**; big numerals (the temperature readout, the phase numerals 01/02/03, the "2027") **1.3x** their 16:9 size, as far as the 840 px safe width allows; overlay numbers likewise. A schematic uses the safe zone fully: **y 230-1150**, x 60-900. The graphic carries a faint dark shadow so it reads on any backdrop.
- **Captions (safe area):** centred on **y ≈ 1250**; **600 px stay empty at the bottom** (nothing below y 1320) and **180 px stay empty on the right** (nothing right of x 900); **at most 2 lines**, about 20 characters per line, Inter Medium 48 px on a soft dark pill. Captions follow the narration (timing from `subtitles_en.srt`).
- **Hook (first 2 seconds):** a big visual hook at the top of the picture, on a legible **dark panel** (near-black, ~93% opaque, fading out at its lower edge, y 0-780): one number (Inter Light, very large) or a short claim of at most 6 words, with an amber hairline and an optional small caps line in teal. It must come from the script and be supported by its sources.
- **End card (last 2 seconds):** "Full episode on the channel" (Inter Medium, 84 px) over a dimmed picture, with "Rebel Minds: Cosmos" in grey capitals beneath.
- **Sound:** narration at **-14 LUFS**, music as in the Music section (about 20 dB under the narration).
- **Packaging:** each Short has a vertical cover brief (1080x1920, key content away from the bottom 600 px and the right 180 px), an English title (max 70 characters), description and pinned comment, all in `yayin_paketi.md`. Sober and scientifically accurate, like everything else.

## Schematic graphics
Key facts are shown as drawn line graphics that build themselves on screen (lines draw, markers slide, numerals count up):
- Timelines for plans and schedule slips (planned vs. now), scales for comparisons (e.g. temperature), orbits and lattices for physical ideas.
- Axes and ticks in grey, the subject in teal, the change or the warning in muted amber.
- Every graphic names its source in the bottom-right source line.
- Draw only numbers that are in the script and its sources. Do not invent positions or dates; if an exact value is unknown, use a bracket or range, not a point.

## On-screen text (must be legible on a phone)
- Big numbers: Inter Light, very large, with a hairline rule underneath and a one-line explanation in Inter Regular. They enter with a rise and un-blur (counting up where it makes sense) and leave the same way.
- Labels, kickers and captions: Inter Medium, letter-spaced capitals, **at least 36 px on a 1080p frame**. Nothing smaller except the source line.
- Headlines and lower thirds: Inter Medium, at least 60 px, a thin teal bar at the left; max 6 words.
- Everything stays inside 10% safe margins; use a soft dark scrim only when the background is a photograph.
- Few overlays rather than many — only where they help understanding or land a key number.

## Source line
Every scene with a photo or a graphic shows a small, pale-grey source or image credit at the bottom right (for example "Image: NASA/JSC" or "Source: SpacePolicyOnline, Nov 2026"). It fades in a moment after the scene starts and out before it ends.

## Evidence tracker
A recurring graphic at the top left that appears ONLY when a new piece of evidence is introduced, then disappears: an outlined counter circle (the number rolls up), a hairline that draws out, "EVIDENCE" and a short label (36 px) typed in. It folds away after a few seconds. Never permanent clutter.

## Palette & type
- Ground `#05070C`, ice white `#F2F5FF`, teal `#62C2CF` (accent), muted amber `#D9A25B` (highlight), grey `#8A93A6` (axes, context), dim grey `#5E6678`.
- Inter only: Light for big numerals, Regular for explanations, Medium for labels, headlines and tracker.
- Fonts are bundled in the renderer (SIL OFL); do not depend on a network font service.

## Thumbnail
Max 4 words, one focal subject, readable at phone size, built from the palette above (near-black ground, teal and amber accents).

### Cover concepts (3 per episode)
Every episode gets three cover concepts for the main video — **number** (one figure that is in the script), **mystery** (an open question, never a fake threat) and **clean** (one subject, lots of dark space, hairline detail). Each has an English headline of at most 4 words and an English visual brief to paste into Canva. Headlines are sober and scientifically accurate: no "shocking", "proves", "secret", "impossible"; nothing the video does not show. Where a real mission is meant, the brief names the real NASA/ESA/ESO image to upload instead of generating a look-alike. All of it lives, ready to paste, in `bolumler/<kod>/yayin_paketi.md`.

image.reason: Mercury'nin düz ovaları ve kraterli arazisini gösteren JPL görüntüsü, volkanizma anlatımı için kabul edilebilir bir arka plan sağlıyor.

scenes.narration: In September 2026, conference abstracts suggested hints of buried volcanic ash, and of explosive eruptions at bright patches on the surface.
scenes.schematic: Layered cross-section: teal surface, buried amber ash layer, small plume above bright patch; label BURIED ASH; source EPSC 2026 abstracts. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: They also described a tentative, very large cone of volcanic debris inside the Caloris basin.

image.title: The Great Caloris Basin on Mercury
image.reason: Caloris havzasının tamamını gösteren JPL görüntüsü, sahnenin dev darbe havzası anlatımına doğrudan karşılık geliyor.

scenes.narration: Be careful here. These deposits describe explosive volcanism in the past, not activity today, and their ages are uncertain.

image.title: Extensive Smooth Plains on Mercury
image.reason: Mercury'nin sakin, kraterli yuzeyini gosteren limb goruntusu sahnenin 'sakin yuzey' vurgusuna uygun ve sinematik bir acilis sagliyor.

scenes.narration: These are also conference abstracts, not peer reviewed papers. Nobody has seen an eruption happening.

image.title: SDO Spots Extra Energy in the Sun's Corona [detail]
image.reason: Gunes atmosferinin renkli aktif bolge detayi koronal sahneye yakin, ancak uygun bir video klip bulunamadi.

scenes.narration: So where does that leave the label, dead planet? Let's be exact.

image.title: From Orbit, Looking toward Mercury's Horizon
image.reason: 2016 transit klipleri Merkur'u Gunes diski uzerinde kucuk bir nokta olarak gosterdigi ve anlatim (gezegen etiketi) ile ilgisi olmadigi icin reddedildi; karanlik uzayda Merkur limb'ini gosteren MESSENGER karesi (GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001918) korundu.

scenes.narration: Landforms. Chemistry. Counts of small features. All of it is indirect.
scenes.motion: slow parallax drift, icons enter one by one

image.title: MESSENGER Gathers Unprecedented Data about Mercury Surface
image.reason: MESSENGER'in kraterli yuzey mozaigi 'yer sekilleri' (landforms) fikrini net bir sekilde gorsellestiriyor.

scenes.narration: Nobody has seen an eruption, a new cliff, or a new streak form.

image.title: It All Ends at Mercury Limb
image.reason: Mercury limb'ini sessiz bir uzay gorunumunde gosteren fotograf sahnenin 'sakin ufuk' brifine birebir uyuyor.

scenes.narration: So the evidence does not prove Mercury is alive. What it does is put pressure on the word dead.

image.title: Peak-Ring Basin Close-Up from the Second Mercury Flyby
image.reason: Krater zirve halkali havza yakin cekim yuzeyi, sahnenin 'baski hissi ve yavas yakin arazi' brifine uygun.

scenes.narration: The better word may be quiet. And quiet is not the same as finished.

image.title: Hubble Space Telescope,Spitzer Space Telescope
image.reason: Orion Bulutsusu'nun renkli vadi gorunumu 'sakin renkli kozmik manzara' brifine uygun.

scenes.narration: So how do we settle it? BepiColombo is a European and Japanese mission, and only the second ever to orbit Mercury.
scenes.schematic: ESA-only: two orbiter icons (European MPO teal, Japanese Mio amber) beside Mercury, labels EUROPEAN and JAPANESE, SECOND TO ORBIT; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: It launched in 2018, so this arrival took about eight years.

video.title: Observing Comet Siding Spring at Mars
video.reason: Gunes sistemi yorunge animasyonu 'uzun gezegen yolculugu' fikrini metin icermeden gosteriyor.

scenes.narration: ESA says the science phase should start in April 2027, though dates may change.

image.reason: PIA11219 renkli Merkur yarimkuresini gosteriyor ama 2x2 panel, ok ve harf etiketleri iceriyor; PIA11221 ucus plani haritasi, PIA11372 ve GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001870 ise baska sahnelerde kullanildigi icin -1 secildi.

scenes.narration: Now think about what its tools can add. The European orbiter carries a laser altimeter,
scenes.motion: laser line sweeps along the terrain
scenes.schematic: Orbiter icon in teal firing a thin amber laser line down to a teal surface profile; 'Illustration'; label LASER ALTIMETER. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: and study author Nishiyama told the Associated Press that it should confirm the shrinking.

video.title: Hypercolor Mosaic
video.reason: SVS-11197 Merkur'un iki yarimkuresini renkli ve metinsiz gosteren 960x540 klip; kucuk gezegen kesiti icin uygun bir Merkur kuresi sunuyor.

scenes.narration: It also carries a high-resolution camera that can compare today's surface with MESSENGER's images.
scenes.motion: slow pan across, frames slide in

image.title: MESSENGER Departs Mercury
image.reason: MESSENGER'in Merkür'ü yakından gördüğü NAC karesi yüzey bağlamı verir, ancak görüntü çok düşük çözünürlüklüdür.

scenes.narration: And here is the callback. Remember the hollows, young and maybe still forming?

image.title: A Detailed Look at Raditladi Basin
image.reason: Raditladi havzasının MESSENGER MDIS mozaiği, senaryodaki genç ve oluşmakta olabilecek çukur (hollow) bağlamına doğrudan uyan Merkür yüzeyi karesidir.

scenes.narration: That is the kind of camera that could catch one changing.
scenes.schematic: ESA-only: orbiter icon with amber camera cone aimed at a hollow on a teal planet curve; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: The key comparison is MESSENGER, from 2011 to 2015, against BepiColombo, more than a decade later.

image.title: MESSENGER Discovers Volcanoes on Mercury
image.reason: Bölünmüş zaman çizgisi için uygun bir video yok; MESSENGER dönemini temsil eden Merkür yüzeyi fotoğrafı yedek olarak kullanılabilir.

scenes.narration: A second, sharper look. Comparing the two is how we can search for change.
scenes.motion: slow cross-fade wipe between two frames
scenes.schematic: Two overlaid crater outlines, teal older and amber newer, tiny offset; label COMPARE. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: My guess is that if anything changes, it will be small and slow.
scenes.schematic: Tiny amber tick moving a very small distance on a teal line; label SMALL AND SLOW. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: A hollow edge that moved. A streak that was not there before.
scenes.schematic: Hollow outline with amber dashed shift of the edge, then a new amber streak drawing in. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: But it is entirely possible we will see no change at all.

video.title: Cosmic Origins Spectrograph: Large Scale Structure of the Universe
video.reason: Hubble COS arşivindeki yıldız alanı ve toz şeritleri sakin, sinematik bir kozmik kesit sağlar ve 1280x720 çözünürlüğe sahiptir.

scenes.narration: If nothing changes at the camera's resolution, that would at least put limits on how active Mercury can be.

image.title: Detailed Close-up of Mercury Previously Unseen Surface
image.reason: Uygun Merkur klibi yok (KSC klipleri 320x212, SVS-14261 'Leaders in Lidar' baslik kartli, GSFC tutulma klibi Merkur degil); PIA10174 yaklasik 400 m'ye kadar kraterleri gosteren Merkur yuzeyi fotografi oldugu icin yedek olarak secildi.

scenes.narration: Think about what it would mean if the edge of a single hollow had moved.
scenes.motion: slow push-in on a single hollow
scenes.schematic: One hollow outline with amber arrow marking the edge shift; label ONE EDGE. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: Not a theory about the past, but a change we could point to, between two sets of pictures.

video.title: NASA's Fermi Spies a Supercharged Supernova
video.reason: Crab bulutsusunun 4K zaman atlamalı görüntüsü renkli, kozmik ve hareketli olup sahnenin 'renkli bulutsu' talebine tam uyar.

scenes.narration: That one small shift would turn a clue into a measurement.

image.title: Using Reprojections to Examine Mercury Surface
image.reason: PIA12054 Merkur yuzeyinde bir scarp'in krateri kestigi, yazi ve logo icermeyen temiz bir yuzey karesi oldugu icin 'olcum' hissi veren sahneye uygun.

scenes.narration: The next step is close. On 9 to 10 December, the two orbiters are due to separate.
scenes.schematic: ESA-only: two orbiter icons moving apart, teal and amber, with dates 9 TO 10 DECEMBER; 'Illustration'. Style: #05070C ground, teal #62C2CF subject, amber #D9A25B highlight, grey axes, Inter labels 36px+, drifting dust.

scenes.narration: The honest answer today is that we do not know yet.

video.reason: Kalan adaylarin hepsi ya baska sahnelerde kullanildi (SVS-14110, PIA13477, GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001918) ya da 320x212, baslik karti, Gunes agirlikli veya buyuk metinli; karanlikta sakin bir Merkur gorunumu olmadigi icin -1 secildi.

scenes.narration: If you want to follow the story as the first science images arrive, subscribe to Rebel Minds Cosmos.

image.reason: Renkli Hubble yıldız alanı ve süpernova kalıntısı (N49) görüntüsü kanal tonuna uygun, ancak brief bir hareketli klip istiyor; uygun bir klip bulunamadığı için fotoğraf seçildi.
